Fact.Name: Filing Form 2555 to claim the foreign earned income exclusion (taxpayer attestation)
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's own answer to "Are you filing Form 2555 to claim the foreign earned income exclusion or the foreign housing exclusion/deduction?" Form 2555's own instructions state its scope in one sentence: "If you qualify, you can use Form 2555 to figure your foreign earned income exclusion and your housing exclusion or deduction. You cannot exclude or deduct more than the amount of your foreign earned income for the year" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2555.pdf, page 1).
IT IS THE FACT OF FILING, NOT AN AMOUNT, and that distinction is the reason this path exists separately from ctcOdc /foreignEarnedIncomeExclusion911. IRC 32(c)(1)(C) disqualifies "any individual who claims the benefits of section 911 ... for the taxable year" (26 U.S.C. 32, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section32&num=0&edition=2024) with no dollar threshold anywhere in it, and the Form 1040 instructions put the same rule as a yes/no on the EIC eligibility flowchart: "3. Are you filing Form 2555 (relating to foreign earned income)? ... Yes. STOP You can't take the credit" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 40, a two-column layout in which the word "credit." falls on line 2614). A fact that modelled only the exclusion's size would leave that test with nothing to read.
UNANSWERED IS THE OVERWHELMING CASE AND MUST STAY FREE. This is a brand-new question that no committed scenario answers and that the application does not yet ask. A bare Writable read directly by anything would make that consumer Incomplete on every return in the corpus - the completeness-contagion trap. Nothing reads this path directly; every consumer reads /filesForm2555ForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion below, which resolves Complete-FALSE when this is unanswered.
SCOPE OF THE ATTESTATION. One boolean for the return, not one per filer, because every consumer named in the contracts is return-level: section 32(c)(1)(C) disqualifies the return's EITC outright, the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 2a reads "your (and your spouse's if filing jointly) Form 2555, lines 45 and 50" - a joint figure - and Form 8960 line 13's add-back is a single MAGI adjustment. A per-filer split would have to be re-collapsed at every one of them.

Fact.Name: The filer claims the Form 2555 foreign earned income exclusion (the representability gate)
Fact.Description:
/writableFilesForm2555ForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion when ANSWERED, else FALSE - the IsComplete/Switch guard idiom (the same shape as iraDeduction:/mfsSpouseCoveredByEmployerPlanComplete and formW2s:/formW2s/*/oasdiWages). THIS is the path every Form 2555 carve-out in this graph switches on; the writable above is never read directly.
FALSE RATHER THAN THE USUAL CONSERVATIVE TRUE, deliberately. On this gate, TRUE is the answer that costs the taxpayer their EITC and adds back their exclusion to NIIT MAGI, so defaulting unanswered to TRUE would deny a credit to every filer in the corpus who has simply never been asked. FALSE is also the only value that keeps every committed scenario byte-identical, which is the world-1 requirement here. The price of FALSE - that a Form 2555 filer who is never asked the question is silently treated as not filing - is paid by /knockoutFilesForm2555 below only for filers who ANSWER yes, and is NOT paid for a filer who is never asked at all. That residual is the application pickup named in the module comment: until the question is asked, this dictionary cannot distinguish "no Form 2555" from "not asked", and the honest statement of that is this paragraph rather than a knockout the dictionary has no input to fire.
CONSUMERS, and their current state, because a gate whose consumers are unbuilt must be honest about that. Built and shipping: /knockoutFilesForm2555 below; eitc /maybeEligibleForEitcBase (IRC 32(c)(1)(C), a total disqualification); the two Schedule 1 AGI legs /schedule1Line8dForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion and /schedule1Line24jHousingDeduction, which switch on this path so that no gate-false return's AGI can move; and form8960 /niitMagiForeignEarnedIncomeAddback (Form 8960 line 13), which reads THIS path as its own entry gate, for the reason its Description gives: the exclusion aliases are ungated, so an ungated add-back would restore an amount that never left AGI. Its sibling obligation is discharged the required way: preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetTax (the Form 1040 line-16 rate-stacking worksheet, for the unstarred route) reads THIS path as its entry gate, not a local boolean. The knockout is what makes shipping ahead of it safe: no return that asserts the gate is computable, so it cannot be silently wrong for one.
TYPE: Boolean; no sign or rounding.

Fact.Name: Knockout: the return claims the Form 2555 foreign earned income exclusion
Fact.Description:
Refuses any return that answers the Form 2555 attestation YES, for as long as the section 911 computation is unbuilt. Dual-wired in the module's own idiom (its own BlockSubmissionOnTrue plus membership in flow:/flowIsKnockedOut).
UNCONDITIONAL ON THE GATE - no amount threshold, no state condition, no filing-status condition - and that is load-bearing, not stylistic. The unbuilt consumers move tax in BOTH directions for this population: the section 32(c)(1)(C) EITC disqualification and the Form 8960 line-13 MAGI add-back are taxpayer-UNFAVOURABLE, and the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet's rate stacking is taxpayer-UNFAVOURABLE too while the exclusion itself is favourable. A conditional refusal would leave some Form 2555 return computable with all of them missing, which is the failure this knockout exists to prevent. Any narrowing of this condition must land in the same commit as the computation that makes the narrowed population correct.
WHY A SEPARATE FACT RATHER THAN BlockSubmissionOnTrue ON THE GATE ITSELF. The gate is a long-lived path that seven modules read; the refusal is temporary and retires separately. Keeping them separate makes the retirement a one-fact deletion (plus its flow.xml membership) instead of surgery on a fact with seven consumers, and keeps the gate free of a submission-blocking side effect that its consumers do not want. It also matches the module-local knockout idiom every sibling uses (form4684 /knockoutCasualtyGain, foreignTaxCredit /knockoutForeignTaxRequiresForm1116).
WORLD-1: refuses rather than filing a foreign-earned-income return whose EITC, whose NIIT MAGI and whose Form 1040 line 16 are each computed as though no exclusion existed. No committed scenario answers the attestation, so this fact is FALSE everywhere today and /flowIsKnockedOut is byte-identical.
RETIREMENT TRIGGER, so a future reviewer does not have to reconstruct it. FIVE of the thirteen original conditions are discharged; eight remain and are load-bearing:
DISCHARGED: 1. preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetTax computes the Form 1040 line-16 rate stacking (taxpayer-UNFAVOURABLE when absent, so its absence under-states tax). All three routes of the worksheet's line 4 COMPUTE — unstarred, the QDCGT starred arm, and the Schedule D Tax Worksheet starred arm — and the preferential-rate knockout retired with no residue (the Form 4952 line-4g disjunct ships in scheduleD:/useScheduleDTaxWorksheet, and its line-3/line-4 inputs flow through both the ordinary and Form-2555 Schedule D Tax Worksheet runs). Kept numbered because the ordering of these conditions is cited from three other files; 2. form8960 /niitMagiForeignEarnedIncomeAddback and form8960 /niitMagi carry Form 8960 line 13 as AGI plus the section 911(a)(1) exclusion net of Form 2555 line 44, gated on THIS module's attestation and floored at zero, off the printed Line 13-MAGI Worksheet (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8960.pdf, page 23). Needed no new intake: both terms are Form 2555 entries this module already collects. Kept numbered for the same reason as condition 1; 3. THE AGI LEG. A filer no longer enters an exclusion that never reduces their AGI - see the AGI LEG block comment below. Kept numbered for the same reason as condition 1. What it did NOT discharge is condition 6, which it created; 4. Parts VII/IX's caps and entry conditions. PART VII IS DISCHARGED: lines 37-42 are built below and /foreignEarnedIncomeExclusion911 is the line-42 entry capped at the smaller of the prorated $130,000 (lines 37/38/39/40) and foreign earned income less the housing exclusion (line 41), with the line-34 employer-provided ceiling enforced on /form2555Line36HousingExclusion at the same time. Three optional writables (lines 27, 34 and 38) are what the caps needed; six node tests pin them. PART IX'S ARITHMETIC IS BUILT; ITS POPULATION QUESTION IS NOT, AND THAT IS CONDITION 7. Notice 2025-16 is vendored and module form2555Housing carries lines 28-36 and 46-50 off it: the per-locality line-29b limit, the base housing amount, the line-35 ratio, and a line 49 allowed up to line 47 minus line 48 (the IRC 911(c)(4)(C) limitation, not also gated on the printed Part IX heading, per owner ruling NE-7). /form2555Line50HousingDeduction prefers that computed line 50 and falls back to the faithful uncapped entry only where the computation is incomplete; AND 6. THE SECTION 911 MAGI ADD-BACKS. Kept numbered for the same reason as condition 1. Both surfaces this condition names carry the section 911 add-back: socialSecurity /socialSecurityBenefitsWkshtLine3 reads ctcOdc:/sched8812Line2bForm2555Exclusions, which IS /form2555Lines45And50ForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2a - the very figure this condition names; taxCalculations /magiForIraDeduction reads the same ctcOdc:/sched8812Line2bForm2555Exclusions directly in its own leaf list (it is built from the same acyclic leaves the worksheet line 3 uses, never from that fact), and section 219(g)(3)(A)(ii) names section 911 (26 U.S.C. 219, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section219&num=0&edition=2024), so the add-back is CORRECT for that MAGI rather than incidental. It carries no section 931 or 933 add-back, because section 219(g)(3)(A)(ii) names neither; its own Description records that. Its leaf list has no socialSecurity worksheet line 3 source and no section 931 or 933 term (the argument for verify row FED-1040-IRADED-F2555KOPROSE-045, ARGUE; IRC 219(g)(3)(A)(ii), 26 U.S.C. 219, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section219&num=0&edition=2024).
NOT DISCHARGED - conditions 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 13, all load-bearing: 5. The application asks the questions. THIS CONDITION IS NOT DISCHARGEABLE IN THIS REPO - the intake surface lives in SERVICE (invariant #7's frontend clause), so no computation built here can retire this guard however much of it computes. A finding that condition 4 is fully discharged should say so and STILL leave the knockout up; AND 7. THE SECOND HOUSING CHAIN FOR SPOUSES WHO DO NOT SHARE A FOREIGN HOUSEHOLD. The housing chain in module form2555Housing is one chain per RETURN. That is exactly what the instructions prescribe for the default regime, spouses sharing a foreign household and figuring jointly - "either spouse (but not both) can claim ... aggregate the housing expenses of both spouses ... subtract their base housing amount" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2555.pdf, page 5) - and married filing separately is right by construction, each return being its own graph instance. The other two regimes need a SECOND parallel chain and there is none. Spouses figuring separately "must figure the housing amounts separately using such spouse's respective base housing amount" (lines 315-318), and spouses living outside reasonable commuting distance of one another may each "claim qualified expenses for your own household" (lines 321-327). Each of those needs its own qualifying period, its own line 29b limit, its own base housing amount and its own housing-location collection - a per-filer index that neither this module nor form2555Housing has. On a joint return where both spouses separately qualify and keep separate foreign households, the second spouse's housing exclusion and deduction are unavailable and that spouse's housing amount stays in AGI: taxpayer-ADVERSE. This is a POPULATION question, not an arithmetic one. Retiring this knockout without settling it files a joint return that silently drops one spouse's housing chain, and it is the reason the knockout must not be narrowed to "returns that claim a housing amount" as a halfway step. The population now also has its own refusal, form2555Housing:/knockoutForm2555SpousesHousingFiguredSeparatelyUnbuilt, which keeps it refused after this blanket retires, so retiring this condition means building the second chain, not dropping the refusal; AND 8. THE ADDITIONAL CHILD TAX CREDIT IS DENIED TO A SECTION 911 CLAIMANT AND NOTHING IMPLEMENTS THE DENIAL. Section 24(d)(3), "(3) Exception for taxpayers excluding foreign" earned income (26 U.S.C. 24, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section24&num=0&edition=2024), turns the refundable limb OFF for any taxpayer who elects a section 911 exclusion. ctcOdc DOES read this module, twice (the Credit Limit Worksheet B trigger's limb 2, "not filing Form 2555", and Schedule 8812 line 2b in ctcOdc), but /additionalCtc's own body is a two-arm Switch over /writableDoesNotWantToClaimActc, /remainingPotentialActc and /maximumActc and carries NO Form 2555 dependency, and no fact in that chain implements the subsection (d)(3) exception. So a section 911 claimant is paid an ACTC the statute denies: taxpayer-FAVOURABLE and MONEY OUT OF THE TREASURY, not tax merely uncollected. NOT BUILT; it is open and the fix lives in dictionary/ty2025/ctcOdc.xml, not here; AND 9. THE MAXIMUM EXCLUSION IS PER INDIVIDUAL AND THIS MODULE APPLIES ONE CEILING PER RETURN. Section 911(b)(2)(A) limits "the foreign earned income of an individual" (26 U.S.C. 911, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section911&num=0&edition=2024) and the instructions say to figure the exclusion separately for each spouse on separate Forms 2555 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2555.pdf, page 6). Every fact in the lines 37/39/40/41/42 chain below is return-level and none of them touches /filers/*, so a joint return on which both spouses qualify gets ONE maximum exclusion instead of two: taxpayer-ADVERSE, by up to a second full ceiling. It is the same missing per-filer index as condition 7 and it is stated separately because the two fail on different lines and in opposite directions. NOT BUILT; it is open and the fix is in THIS file and in form2555Housing.xml; AND 10. EXCLUDED FOREIGN EARNED INCOME IS NOT IRA COMPENSATION. Section 219(b)(1)(B) caps the deduction at "(B) an amount equal to the compensation" includible in the individual's gross income (26 U.S.C. 219, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section219&num=0&edition=2024), and an excluded amount is by definition not includible. iraDeduction:/primaryFilerIraCompensation reads the wage and self-employment base with no section 911 subtraction, so a filer who excludes the income keeps the full compensation ceiling: taxpayer-FAVOURABLE. Witnessed by node test form2555/f2555-agi-leg-gate-true-full-movement, which excludes 125,000 and still resolves /primaryFilerIraCompensation to 150,000. NOT BUILT; it is open and the fix lives in dictionary/ty2025/iraDeduction.xml; AND 11. THE AMT LIMB OF THE RATE-STACKING RULE. Section 911(f)(1)(B) applies the same stacking to the alternative minimum tax - "if such taxpayer has a taxable excess" (26 U.S.C. 911, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section911&num=0&edition=2024), the Form 6251 counterpart of the section 1 limb that condition 1 discharged. form6251:/tentativeMinimumTax and the /amtBaseOverExemption chain compute from an AMT base that never adds the exclusion back, and the form's own printed Form 2555 sentences on lines 20 and 27 are not reached in form6251. So the AMT a section 911 claimant owes is under-stated: taxpayer-FAVOURABLE. NOT BUILT; it is open and the fix lives in dictionary/ty2025/form6251.xml and dictionary/ty2025/preferentialRateTax.xml; AND 12. THE SAVER'S CREDIT AGI IS DETERMINED WITHOUT REGARD TO SECTION 911. Section 25B(e): "For purposes of this section, adjusted gross income shall be determined without regard to sections 911, 931, and 933." (26 U.S.C. 25B, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section25B&num=0&edition=2024). saversCredits:/isAgiEligibleForSaversCredit and its three filing-status siblings read taxCalculations:/agi with no add-back, so the exclusion can buy an eligibility the statute withholds: taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, and refundable-adjacent in the sense that it is a credit the filer is not entitled to. Witnessed by node test form2555/f2555-agi-leg-gate-true-full-movement, whose AGI is 25,000 only because 125,000 of section 911 exclusions came out of it and whose /isAgiEligibleForSaversCredit is TRUE; on the statute's AGI of 150,000 it is not. NOT BUILT; it is open and the fix lives in dictionary/ty2025/saversCredits.xml; AND 13. THE PREMIUM TAX CREDIT HOUSEHOLD-INCOME ADD-BACK. Section 36B(d)(2)(B)(i) builds modified AGI by adding "(i) any amount excluded from gross income under section 911," (26 U.S.C. 36B, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section36B&num=0&edition=2024). ptc:/ptcMagi carries the tax-exempt interest and non-taxable social security terms and NOT the section 911 term, so a section 911 claimant's household income is under-stated and the PTC over-paid: taxpayer-FAVOURABLE and, like condition 8, MONEY OUT OF THE TREASURY. UNADJUDICATED - it is listed here as an open question rather than as a settled defect, and whoever adjudicates it owns this condition's wording. NOT BUILT; the surface is dictionary/ty2025/ptc.xml. Retiring it earlier makes a Form 2555 return filable and wrong.
WHAT THIS LIST DOES NOT REACH, recorded so the next reader does not think the ledger question is closed.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a Form 2555 return completes both Part II and Part III, or neither
Fact.Description:
Refuses a return that claims the Form 2555 foreign earned income exclusion but completes BOTH Part II (the bona fide residence test) and Part III (the physical presence test), or NEITHER. The instructions say "You must complete either Part II or Part III of Form 2555, but not both parts", and IRC 911(d)(1) makes the exclusion depend on meeting one of the two tests, so a return with both or neither does not say which test it relies on.
THE OPENING ENTRY OF EACH PART STANDS FOR THE PART: line 10, "Date bona fide residence began", for Part II, and the line 16 "from" date for Part III. Both are free-text writables (/writableForm2555Line10BonaFideResidenceBeganDate, /writableForm2555Line16PhysicalPresencePeriodBeganDate); an entry counts once it is answered. The printed "If an item doesn't apply, enter N/A" (f2555 line 32) governs items INSIDE the part the filer completes; the part not completed is left blank, so the application must not write "N/A" into the other part's opening date.
TRUE when /filesForm2555ForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion is TRUE and those two entries are both answered or both unanswered; FALSE on every return that does not claim the exclusion, so it is complete on every return. The remedy is a corrected answer: complete the part for the one test the filer meets and leave the other part blank.
ADDITIVE TODAY: /knockoutFilesForm2555 above already refuses every Form 2555 return, so this fact does its work only after that knockout retires. It blocks submission on its own (BlockSubmissionOnTrue) and is a member of flow:/flowIsKnockedOut.

Fact.Name: Foreign earned income entered on Form 2555 line 27 (= line 26)
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's Form 2555 Part V line 27 entry, "Enter the amount from line 26" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3), where line 26 is "Subtract line 25 from line 24 ... This is your 2025 foreign earned income" (line 124). It is the section 911(b)(1) quantity - the income the exclusion is an exclusion OF.
WHY IT IS COLLECTED AND WHAT IT IS NOT. It is collected for ONE purpose: Part VII line 41, "Subtract line 36 from line 27", which is one of the two arms of the line-42 ceiling. It is NOT an income intake: nothing adds it to /totalIncome or to any Form 1040 line. The foreign earned income of a section 911 filer reaches this return through the ordinary wage and self-employment intakes, exactly as it did before; this figure is a CEILING INPUT and is read by /form2555Line41ForeignEarnedIncomeLessHousingExclusion alone. Part IV (lines 19-26, the itemised build-up of foreign earned income) is NOT modelled here - this is the single summary figure the taxpayer carries forward on the paper form, in the same spirit as the four exclusion entries below. HELP: leave out income earned in the United States on business (line 14 column (d) and line 18 column (f)). The Part IV Note says "Don't include income from line 14, column (d), or line 18, column (f)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 2); that income is not foreign earned income and is reported on Form 1040 through the ordinary intakes. The graph cannot net it out of this figure itself, because the entry is the filer's own Part IV total.
Optional - unanswered gives /form2555Line27ForeignEarnedIncome $0, and the line-41 arm of the line-42 ceiling is then not formed at all (the flat prorated line-40 ceiling still binds).

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 27 foreign earned income, complete-safe
Fact.Description:
= /writableForm2555Line27ForeignEarnedIncome when answered, else $0. The same IsComplete/Switch guard idiom every alias in this module uses; the writable is never read outside an IsComplete-guarded arm.
THE $0 TAIL IS NOT A CEILING OF $0. Read on its own this fact resolves $0 for a filer who did not answer, and a naive line-41 arm built on it would compute a ceiling of 0 - 36 = negative and zero a real exclusion. That is why /foreignEarnedIncomeExclusion911 gates the line-41 arm on IsComplete of the WRITABLE and not on this alias being non-zero: an unanswered line 27 must produce NO line-41 ceiling, not a ceiling of zero.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE, whole dollars.

Fact.Name: Employer-provided amounts entered on Form 2555 line 34
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's Form 2555 Part VI line 34 entry, "Enter employer-provided amounts. See instructions" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3). Its only job here is the second sentence of the line-36 caption: "Enter the result but don't enter more than the amount on line 34" (line 148-149). The section 911(a)(2) housing exclusion is an exclusion of employer-provided amounts, so it cannot exceed them - the housing cost that is NOT employer-provided is a housing DEDUCTION at Part IX, not an exclusion.
NOT the line-35 ratio input. The form also divides this by line 27 to get line 35, and line 35 x line 33 is how line 36 is COMPUTED. That computation lives in module form2555Housing (/form2555Line35EmployerProvidedRatioThousandths and /form2555ComputedLine36HousingExclusion), which reads this writable for the ratio and for the line-36 ceiling; /form2555Line36HousingExclusion below also applies it as a ceiling on the fallback entry.
Optional - unanswered means no line-34 ceiling is formed and the line-36 entry stands as entered.

Fact.Name: Days of the qualifying period falling within 2025, entered on Form 2555 line 38
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's Form 2555 Part VII line 38 entry: "If you completed Part VI, enter the number from line 31. All others, enter the number of days in your qualifying period that fall within your 2025 tax year" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3). This is the numerator of the line-39 fraction that prorates the section 911(b)(2)(D) exclusion amount for a filer whose qualifying period does not cover the whole year. The PRORATION itself is section 911(b)(2)(A)'s ("computed on a daily basis at an annual rate equal to the exclusion amount"), not (D)'s - (D) supplies only the annual rate that (A) then spreads over the qualifying days.
WHY THE MAXIMUM IS 366 AND NOT 365. 2025 is not a leap year, so the denominator is 365 and a full-year qualifying period is 365 days. The Max limit is nevertheless 366 rather than 365 because the line-39 caption says "the number of days in your 2025 tax year (usually 365)" - an ordinary (non-52-53-week) fiscal-year filer whose 12-month accounting period spans February 29 of a leap year is a real, if rare, shape (a 52-53-week fiscal year, by contrast, is always 364 or 371 days and never 366), and a Limit that rejected 366 would reject an entry the form's own parenthetical anticipates. The line-39 fraction is capped at 1.000 regardless, exactly as the form directs, so a day count above 365 cannot produce a ceiling above $130,000.
Optional - unanswered means the line-39 fraction defaults to 1.000 (the full-year, no proration case). See THE UNANSWERED-CAP RULE in the banner above for why the default runs that way and not to zero.

Fact.Name: Housing exclusion entered on Form 2555 line 36 (the section 911(a)(2) housing cost amount)
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's Form 2555 Part VI line 36 entry: "Housing exclusion. Multiply line 33 by line 35. Enter the result but don't enter more than the amount on line 34. Also, complete Part VIII" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3). This is the IRC 911(a)(2) half of the section 911 exclusion - "the housing cost amount of such individual" (26 U.S.C. 911, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section911&num=0&edition=2024, a two-column extraction whose subsection heading sits on line 18 and whose text runs 21-29).
THE FALLBACK ENTRY. Part VI lines 28-35 figure this amount from the qualifying period, the base housing amount and employer-provided amounts, and module form2555Housing computes it (/form2555ComputedLine36HousingExclusion). This writable is the figure the taxpayer computed on paper, read by /form2555Line36HousingExclusion only while that computation is incomplete; it enforces only non-negativity itself, and the alias caps it at line 34 when line 34 is answered.
DISTINCT FROM THE HOUSING DEDUCTION at line 50, which is a DEDUCTION and not an exclusion and which Part IX makes mutually exclusive with this line in practice (Part IX is completed "only if (a) line 33 is more than line 36"). Never sum the two into anything named "exclusion": line 50 appears below only inside the lines 45+50 worksheet figure.
Optional - unanswered gives /form2555Line36HousingExclusion $0.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 36 housing exclusion, complete-safe
Fact.Description:
Form 2555 line 36, complete-safe, in this order: $0 when line 27 is answered No (form2555Housing /writableForm2555Line27ClaimingHousingExclusionOrDeduction, "No" goes to Part VII); otherwise form2555Housing /form2555ComputedLine36HousingExclusion when that computation is complete; otherwise /writableForm2555Line36HousingExclusion, capped at line 34 when line 34 is answered; otherwise $0. The IsComplete/Switch guard idiom, the same shape as /filesForm2555ForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion above and form4952 /investmentInterestCarryforwardIn: no writable is read without its guard. $0 when nothing is answered over-states income and therefore over-taxes, the conservative direction.
⚠ THE LINE-34 CEILING IS ENFORCED HERE (retirement condition 4), so this fact is not a bare pass-through. The line-36 caption's second sentence is a cap in as many words - "Enter the result but don't enter more than the amount on line 34" - and nothing in this graph applied it before. When /writableForm2555Line34EmployerProvidedAmounts is answered, this fact is the LESSER of the entry and that amount; when it is unanswered, no ceiling is formed and the entry stands, per THE UNANSWERED-CAP RULE in the module banner. DIRECTION: the cap can only REDUCE the housing exclusion, which RAISES income and tax. Taxpayer-adverse in isolation and correct: an exclusion of employer-provided amounts cannot exceed the employer-provided amounts, and the excess is a housing DEDUCTION at Part IX, not an exclusion. Nothing is silently lost - Part IX is where it belongs, and form2555Housing computes it (see /form2555Line50HousingDeduction). NO SEPARATE CAP FACT: the ceiling is one guarded Switch arm rather than a /form2555Line36...Cap fact, because a cap fact would have to resolve to "no cap" for the unanswered case and the only honest spelling of that is the entry itself, which makes the cap fact read its own consumer's input. The three-arm Switch says the same thing without the circular-looking read.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE, whole dollars. Both operands of the LesserOf carry a Min-0 Limit, so the result cannot go negative.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 37 — the maximum foreign earned income exclusion for 2025
Fact.Description:
Form 2555 line 37, "Maximum foreign earned income exclusion. Enter $130,000" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3). This is IRC 911(b)(2)(D)(i)'s $80,000 statutory figure as adjusted for inflation under 911(b)(2)(D)(ii); the form prints the adjusted 2025 amount, and the form is the authority this dictionary uses for it. A constant, not an entry: the taxpayer copies it off the form.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, whole dollars, positive.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 39 — the qualifying-period fraction, in thousandths
Fact.Description:
Form 2555 line 39: "If line 38 and the number of days in your 2025 tax year (usually 365) are the same, enter 1.000. Otherwise, divide line 38 by the number of days in your 2025 tax year and enter the result as a decimal (rounded to at least three places)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3). Carried as an integer count of THOUSANDTHS - 1.000 is 1000, 0.756 is 756 - so the printed three-place decimal needs no fractional type. /form2555Line40ProratedMaximumExclusion divides by 1000 again.
CAPPED AT 1.000 even though the form states the cap only implicitly (line 39's first bullet is an equality case, not a ceiling). The cap is what makes the line-38 Max limit of 366 safe: a fiscal-year day count above 365 would otherwise produce a fraction above 1 and a ceiling above the statutory maximum, which is the one thing this whole block exists to prevent.
UNANSWERED DEFAULTS TO 1000, i.e. NO PRORATION. This is the single exception to the unanswered-cap rule in the module banner, and the reason is stated there: the flat $130,000 ceiling must bind on every answered exclusion, so its input cannot be allowed to suppress it - but defaulting the day count to ZERO would zero a real exclusion for a filer who answered the exclusion question and was never asked the day count. Defaulting to the FULL YEAR yields the largest lawful ceiling and can only ever fail to catch a proration, never invent one.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar carrying thousandths (an integer 0-1000), rounded HALF_UP at the third decimal place of the underlying fraction.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 40 — the maximum exclusion prorated by the qualifying period
Fact.Description:
Form 2555 line 40, "Multiply line 37 by line 39" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3) = $130,000 x the line-39 fraction, undone from thousandths by the /1000 and rounded to whole dollars. This is the section 911(b)(2)(A) ceiling - the (D) exclusion amount spread over the days - as it applies to THIS taxpayer's qualifying period, and it is the arm of the line-42 ceiling that binds unconditionally - the other arm (line 41) needs an answered line 27.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, whole dollars, non-negative. One Round, placed where the form places it (after the multiplication by the already-rounded fraction), so the two roundings compose exactly as the paper form's do.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 41 — foreign earned income less the housing exclusion
Fact.Description:
Form 2555 line 41, "Subtract line 36 from line 27" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3). The second arm of the line-42 ceiling, and the arithmetic reason section 911 cannot exclude more than it earned: whatever the housing exclusion already took out of foreign earned income is not available to the foreign earned income exclusion as well.
READS THE CAPPED LINE 36, not the raw entry, because the form's line 41 reads its own line 36 and this module's line 36 IS the capped alias. No cycle: line 36's own body reads only its entry and line 34, never line 42 or anything downstream of it.
NO FLOOR, faithful to the printed subtraction. A negative result is arithmetically reachable (an entered housing exclusion larger than entered foreign earned income) and is a taxpayer data error rather than a modelling case; it is handled where it matters, at /foreignEarnedIncomeExclusion911, whose GreaterOf keeps the exclusion non-negative. Putting the floor here instead would silently convert a contradictory pair of entries into a ceiling of exactly zero and hide it.
UNANSWERED LINE 27 does NOT suppress this fact - the complete-safe alias gives $0 and this fact resolves to -line36. That value is never read in that case: the consumer gates the line-41 arm on IsComplete of the line-27 WRITABLE, precisely so an unanswered line 27 produces no ceiling rather than a ceiling of zero.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, SIGNED.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 42 as the form computes it — the smaller of line 40 and line 41
Fact.Description:
Form 2555 line 42, "Foreign earned income exclusion. Enter the smaller of line 40 or line 41" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3). This fact is the form's OWN line 42 - the largest exclusion this taxpayer may lawfully claim - and it is used as a CEILING on the taxpayer's entry rather than as a replacement for it. The distinction matters and is deliberate: a filer may claim LESS than the maximum, and the entry is the claim.
VALID ONLY WHEN LINE 27 IS ANSWERED, because line 41 is. The consumer /foreignEarnedIncomeExclusion911 gates on IsComplete of the line-27 writable and falls back to /form2555Line40ProratedMaximumExclusion alone when it is not answered; this fact still RESOLVES in that case (line 41 is -line36 and this is the lesser of the two), and that resolved value is deliberately not read. Stated because a reader who sees this fact Complete on an unanswered-line-27 case would otherwise reasonably assume it is live.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, SIGNED (it inherits line 41's sign).

Fact.Name: Foreign earned income exclusion entered on Form 2555 line 42 (the section 911(a)(1) amount)
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's Form 2555 Part VII line 42 entry: "Foreign earned income exclusion. Enter the smaller of line 40 or line 41. Also, complete Part VIII" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3). This is the IRC 911(a)(1) half of the section 911 exclusion - "the foreign earned income of such individual" (26 U.S.C. 911, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section911&num=0&edition=2024).
AN ENTRY, NOT A COMPUTATION, AND DELIBERATELY UNCAPPED. Line 40 is line 37's $130,000 maximum exclusion prorated by the line-39 qualifying-period fraction, and line 41 is foreign earned income (line 27) less the line-36 housing exclusion (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3). NEITHER is modelled: the $130,000 cap and the day-count proration are explicitly out of this node's scope, so this writable accepts the taxpayer's figure and enforces only non-negativity. There is no Limit type="Max" here and its absence is a decision, not an oversight - an entry above $130,000 is wrong on the paper form but is not filable through this graph while /knockoutFilesForm2555 refuses the population. The Part VII cap that WOULD apply here is enforced on /foreignEarnedIncomeExclusion911 (retirement condition 4); this writable stays uncapped by design.
Optional - unanswered gives /foreignEarnedIncomeExclusion911 $0.

Fact.Name: Income excluded under section 911(a)(1) - Form 2555 line 42 ALONE, without the housing exclusion
Fact.Description:
= /writableForm2555Line42ForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion when answered, else $0. THE HUB the section 911 contract specified, SCOPED TO SECTION 911(a)(1) ALONE - the foreign earned income exclusion at Form 2555 line 42, WITHOUT the section 911(a)(2) housing exclusion at line 36. The path name is the statute's own term and the form's own caption, not "the foreign earned income exclusion together with the housing exclusion" - one Dollar demonstrably cannot serve the three consumers that name section 911.
WHICH CONSUMER READS WHICH PATH. This table is the authority; a consumer wired off it is wrong by a known amount in a known direction. * Form 8960 line 13 (NIIT MAGI add-back) reads THIS PATH. The instruction names section 911(a)(1) and nothing else: "you must increase your AGI by the excess of the amount excluded from income under section 911(a)(1) over the amount of any deductions ... or exclusions disallowed under section 911(d)(6)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8960.pdf, page 22). Given line 43 instead it would over-add the housing exclusion. * Form 2441 lines 4/5 (the earned-income subtraction) reads /form2555Line43Section911TotalExclusions, NOT this path - "Excluded as foreign earned income (including any housing exclusion) on Form 2555, line 43" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4). * The Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 2a reads /form2555Lines45And50ForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2a, NOT this path - "your (and your spouse's if filing jointly) Form 2555, lines 45 and 50" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37). * THE SEVEN THREE-TERM MAGI SURFACES READ NEITHER THIS PATH NOR THE LINE-43 FIGURE: they read /form2555Lines45And50ForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2a, not line 43, though Section 24(b)(1) does define MAGI as "adjusted gross income increased by any amount excluded from gross income under section 911, 931, or 933" (26 U.S.C. 24, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section24&num=0&edition=2024), section 25A(d)(2) repeats it verbatim (26 U.S.C. 25A, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section25A&num=0&edition=2024) and section 86(b)(2)(A) reaches the same place from the other side (26 U.S.C. 86, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section86&num=0&edition=2024) - but the IRS implements all three as Form 2555 lines 45 AND 50. Schedule 8812 line 2b prints it: "Enter the amounts from lines 45 and 50 of your Form 2555" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040s8.pdf, page 1), and the four sibling MAGI facts say the same in their own prose ("Puerto Rico income exclusion, Form 2555 lines 45/50, Form 4563 line 15" - /adoptionMagi, /cleanVehicleCurrentYearMagi, /saltMagi, /schedule1AMagi). It is also the only figure that is arithmetically right HERE: this dictionary's AGI is short by line 45 (Schedule 1 line 8d) plus line 50 (line 24j), so lines 45+50 restores the pre-exclusion AGI the statutes describe, while line 43 would over-add the line-44 allocable deductions and drop the housing deduction. * eitc /maybeEligibleForEitcBase reads NEITHER: section 32(c)(1)(C) turns on the FACT of claiming section 911, so it reads the gate /filesForm2555ForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion above.
ITS ONE BY-NAME CONSUMER IS WIRED: form8960 /niitMagiForeignEarnedIncomeAddback reads THIS path (minus Form 2555 line 44, floored at zero, gated on /filesForm2555ForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion) and is the only fact in the dictionary that does. Form 2441 lines 4/5 and the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet read the OTHER two figures, as do the seven MAGI surfaces. /knockoutFilesForm2555 is what makes the remaining gaps safe rather than silent.
THIS AMOUNT STILL DOES NOT REACH /agi. The AGI leg routes Form 2555 line 45 to Schedule 1 line 8d and line 50 to line 24j (/schedule1Line8dForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion and /schedule1Line24jHousingDeduction). THIS path, the section 911(a)(1) figure, is on NEITHER leg: line 45 is built from line 43, which is line 36 + line 42, so line 42 reaches AGI only through those sums and never as itself. That asymmetry is exactly why the Form 8960 add-back is gated: the amount it adds back is not the amount that came out, and only the gate keeps the two populations the same.
⚠ THE PART VII CEILING IS ENFORCED HERE (the load-bearing clause of retirement condition 4). This fact is the line-42 entry CAPPED at what Form 2555 Part VII allows, and the Part VII block above builds the ceiling. Two arms, and which arms are live depends on what the taxpayer answered: * BOTH LINE 42 AND LINE 27 ANSWERED - the ceiling is the form's own line 42, /form2555Line42MaximumAllowableExclusion = the smaller of line 40 (the prorated $130,000) and line 41 (foreign earned income less the housing exclusion). * LINE 42 ANSWERED, LINE 27 NOT - the line-41 arm cannot be formed, so the ceiling is /form2555Line40ProratedMaximumExclusion alone. The flat statutory ceiling ALWAYS binds on an answered entry; only the income arm is optional. * LINE 42 NOT ANSWERED - $0, exactly as before. THE GreaterOf FLOOR is what keeps the type guarantee below true. Line 41 carries no floor (see that fact), so a taxpayer who enters a housing exclusion larger than their foreign earned income produces a negative ceiling; without the floor this exclusion would go negative and ADD income through the Schedule 1 line-8d leg. The floor turns a contradictory pair of entries into a zero exclusion, which is the conservative direction and the one the module's $0 tails already use everywhere else. DIRECTION OF THE WHOLE CHANGE: the ceiling can only REDUCE an exclusion, i.e. RAISE income and tax. Taxpayer-adverse and correct - the excess was never lawful. It moves no committed scenario, because no committed scenario answers any Form 2555 question.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (an exclusion amount), whole dollars.

Fact.Name: Deductions allocable to excluded income entered on Form 2555 line 44
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's Form 2555 Part VIII line 44 entry: "Deductions allowed in figuring your adjusted gross income (Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11) that are allocable to the excluded income. See instructions and attach computation" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3). An ENTRY with an attached paper computation, which is why nothing here derives it.
NOT THE SAME QUANTITY AS FOREIGN EARNED INCOME TAX WORKSHEET LINE 2b, and conflating the two is the specific error the worksheet's contract warns about. Line 44 is ABOVE-THE-LINE deductions that were ALLOWED in figuring AGI and are allocable to excluded income; worksheet line 2b is "the total amount of any itemized deductions or exclusions you couldn't claim because they are related to excluded income" - DISALLOWED amounts. Line 2b has no path anywhere in this dictionary and the worksheet's own fill owes one.
WHERE IT IS USED, AND WHERE IT MUST NOT BE. It is subtracted exactly once, inside /form2555Line45ExclusionsNetOfAllocableDeductions below, which is itself a term of the lines 45+50 worksheet figure. Form 2441's line-43 figure and the three-term MAGI figure are GROSS of it by their own instruction, so /form2555Line43Section911TotalExclusions does not read it.
Optional - unanswered gives /form2555Line44DeductionsAllocableToExcludedIncome $0.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 44 deductions allocable to excluded income, complete-safe
Fact.Description:
= /writableForm2555Line44DeductionsAllocableToExcludedIncome when answered, else $0. The IsComplete/Switch guard idiom; the writable is never read directly.
THE $0 TAIL RUNS THE OTHER WAY ON THIS ONE, and it is stated rather than assumed. Line 44 is SUBTRACTED at line 45, so an unanswered $0 makes line 45 LARGER, which makes the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet's line 2a larger and its rate stacking HARSHER - the conservative direction for that worksheet, which is a tax-increasing device. It is the taxpayer-adverse direction only in the sense that it withholds a reduction the taxpayer did not claim, and no return can currently reach it at all.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE, whole dollars.

Fact.Name: Housing deduction entered on Form 2555 line 50 (a DEDUCTION, not an exclusion)
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's Form 2555 Part IX line 50 entry: "Housing deduction. Add lines 48 and 49. Enter the total here and on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 24j. Complete the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the Instructions for Form 1040 if you enter an amount on this line" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3).
IT IS NOT AN EXCLUSION AND MUST NEVER BE SUMMED INTO ONE. Part IX is completed "only if (a) line 33 is more than line 36, and (b) line 27 is more than line 43" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3) - i.e. it is the route for housing costs that the line-36 EXCLUSION could not absorb, which makes it mutually exclusive with a full line-36 exclusion in practice. Neither of those two entry conditions is enforced on this entry; the computed line 50 in form2555Housing enforces both, and /form2555Line50HousingDeduction reads this entry only while that computation is incomplete. It appears in exactly one derived fact below, /form2555Lines45And50ForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2a, because the worksheet's own line 2a names it; it is absent from line 43 and from the section 911(a)(1) hub.
Optional - unanswered gives /form2555Line50HousingDeduction $0.

Fact.Description:
Form 2555 line 50, complete-safe, in this order: $0 when line 27 is answered No (form2555Housing /writableForm2555Line27ClaimingHousingExclusionOrDeduction); otherwise form2555Housing /form2555ComputedLine50HousingDeduction (line 48 plus the gated line-49 carryover) when that computation is complete; otherwise /writableForm2555Line50HousingDeduction, floored at $0; otherwise $0. The IsComplete/Switch guard idiom; no writable is read without its guard. $0 when nothing is answered withholds a deduction, which over-states income and over-taxes - the conservative direction.
THE SCHEDULE 1 LINE 24j LEG THIS AMOUNT OWES (module banner). /schedule1Line24jHousingDeduction at the foot of this module passes this figure through unnegated - line 24j is an adjustment, not an income entry - and taxCalculations:/adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanAndIra reads it at the Schedule 1 line-25 slot, so it reaches /adjustmentsToIncome and reduces /agi.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE, whole dollars.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 43 - the WHOLE section 911(a) exclusion (line 36 + line 42), gross of line 44
Fact.Description:
Form 2555 line 43 = "Add lines 36 and 42" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3): the housing exclusion (section 911(a)(2)) plus the foreign earned income exclusion (section 911(a)(1)). GROSS - the line-44 allocable deductions are subtracted at line 45, not here.
THIS IS THE STATUTE-WIDE FIGURE, and it has TWO distinct consumer families, which is why it is a named fact rather than an inline sum: * Form 2441 lines 4/5 subtract exactly this line by name - "Excluded as foreign earned income (including any housing exclusion) on Form 2555, line 43" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2441.pdf, page 4). * The SEVEN three-term MAGI surfaces DO NOT read this line. Measured by DEPENDENCY EDGE, not by prose: across dictionary/ty2025/*.xml there is exactly ONE Dependency edge on this path outside this module, and it is not a MAGI surface at all - form2555Housing.xml's Part IX line 47 (line 27 less line 43). The MAGI family reads /form2555Lines45And50ForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2a, whose two real edges are ctcOdc /sched8812Line2bForm2555Exclusions (from which /dependentCreditMagi, scheduleA /saltMagi via /modifiedAgiWithForeignAndPossessionExclusions, socialSecurity /socialSecurityBenefitsWkshtLine3, taxCalculations /magiForIraDeduction and /magiForStudentLoanInterestDeduction all inherit) and preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2a. The statutory reason the old sentence gave is still true and is kept below, because it is the reason the figure they read is NET of line 44 rather than this gross one: every one of them names section 911 WHOLE and not 911(a)(1): section 24(b)(1) ("increased by any amount excluded from gross income under section 911, 931, or 933", 26 U.S.C. 24, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section24&num=0&edition=2024), section 25A(d)(2), the same formula verbatim (26 U.S.C. 25A, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section25A&num=0&edition=2024), section 86(b)(2)(A) ("without regard to this section and sections 85(c), 135, 137, 221, 911, 931, and 933", 26 U.S.C. 86, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section86&num=0&edition=2024), and the four sibling MAGI facts /adoptionMagi, /cleanVehicleCurrentYearMagi, /saltMagi and /schedule1AMagi. Those surfaces (all but taxCalculations /magiForIraDeduction, whose section 219(g)(3)(A)(ii) list names neither) sum this with the section 931 and section 933 exclusions, which are NOT Form 2555 paths and are not built. Form 8960 line 13 does NOT read this path - it names section 911(a)(1) alone and reads /foreignEarnedIncomeExclusion911.
ONE CONSUMER FAMILY IS WIRED, ONE IS NOT. The MAGI family IS wired, through /form2555Lines45And50ForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2a and not through this path (see the bullet above). And schedule1A has since shipped two facts that read lines 45 and 50 directly - /schedule1ALine2bForm2555Line45Exclusions and /schedule1ALine2cForm2555Line50HousingDeduction. The Form 2441 family is the one that is genuinely unwired, and /knockoutFilesForm2555 is what keeps THAT gap a refusal rather than a wrong number.
WHY THE STALE SENTENCES MATTERED, and why this correction is worth its space: this Description is where an author goes to decide which of the three section 911 figures to wire a NEW consumer to, and it pointed the MAGI family at the gross line-43 figure. Had the author of the two schedule1A facts trusted it instead of the reader table 290 lines up, they would have read line 43 and over-added the line-44 allocable deductions.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: both terms are complete-safe aliases, so this resolves $0 on every return that has answered nothing, which is every committed scenario.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (a sum of two non-negative entries), rounded to whole dollars at this line.

Fact.Name: The Form 2555 line 45 write-in: income earned in a prior year, excluded under the prior-year rule
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's WRITE-IN to the left of Form 2555 line 45. The 2025 Instructions for Form 2555, under the heading Income earned in prior year, carve a whole category of foreign earned income OUT of Part IV and put it here instead: "Foreign earned income received in 2025 for services you performed in 2024 can be excluded from your 2025 gross income if, and to the extent, the income would have been excludable if you had received it in 2024. If you are excluding income under this rule, do not include this income in Part IV. Instead, attach a statement to Form 2555 showing how you figured the exclusion. Enter the amount that would have been excludable in 2024 on Form 2555 to the left of line 45. Next to the amount, enter 'Exclusion of Income Earned in 2024.' Include it in the total reported on line 45" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2555.pdf, page 4). The printed Part IV Note points at the same rule (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 2).
AN ENTRY WITH AN ATTACHED PAPER COMPUTATION, which is why nothing here derives it. What would have been excludable in 2024 depends on the 2024 return's own qualifying period, its own maximum exclusion and its own foreign earned income, none of which this graph holds. It is the same shape as line 44 next door and as the four Part VIII/IX entries above: a faithful uncapped entry.
WHY IT IS A NEW PATH AND NOT A TERM OF AN EXISTING ONE. The two wrong places to put it are both live paths: * NOT /form2555Line43Section911TotalExclusions. Line 43 is "Add lines 36 and 42" and is the figure Form 2441 lines 4/5 subtract BY NAME. The prior-year amount is neither a line-36 housing exclusion nor a line-42 foreign earned income exclusion, and adding it to line 43 would move a Form 2441 number the instruction never touches. * NOT Part IV (lines 19 through 23). The instruction is explicit that the amount does not go there, and putting it there would inflate lines 24/26/27 and with them the line-41 ceiling and the whole Part VI housing chain - wrong in the other direction. So it enters at line 45, exactly once, and reaches the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 2a and the Schedule 1 line-8d leg through /form2555Line45ExclusionsNetOfAllocableDeductions and through nothing else.
TWO CONSUMER QUESTIONS THIS MODULE DOES NOT ANSWER, because they belong to other modules: * Form 8960 line 13 reads /foreignEarnedIncomeExclusion911 (the line-42 figure alone, because the instruction names section 911(a)(1) and nothing else). Whether the prior-year amount belongs in that add-back is form8960's question. * Form 2441 lines 4/5 read /form2555Line43Section911TotalExclusions, which stays gross of this write-in for the reason above. Whether Form 2441's earned-income subtraction owes it is cdcc's question, and it is already an open question there.
Optional - unanswered gives /form2555Line45PriorYearEarnedIncomeExclusion $0, which is the shipping behaviour for every return that does not use the prior-year rule, i.e. every committed scenario.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (an exclusion amount; the Min Limit below DECLARES that bound - Limit enforcement is a JVM-side gate leg (GATE_JVM=1) and the default Scala.js path does not refuse a negative entry, so no derived fact here relies on it), whole dollars.

Fact.Description:
= /writableForm2555Line45PriorYearEarnedIncomeExclusion when answered, else $0. The IsComplete/Switch guard idiom; the writable is never read directly.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 45 - line 43 less line 44, PLUS the prior-year write-in, the figure the paper form routes to Schedule 1 line 8d
Fact.Description:
Form 2555 line 45 = "Subtract line 44 from line 43. Enter the result here and on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8d. Complete the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the Instructions for Form 1040 if you enter an amount on this line" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3).
THE PRINTED SUBTRACTION IS NOT THE WHOLE BODY. This fact is Round(Add(Subtract(line 43, line 44), /form2555Line45PriorYearEarnedIncomeExclusion)). The third term is the WRITE-IN the instructions put to the left of this line for income earned in a prior year, and the instruction says to include it in the total REPORTED ON LINE 45 rather than anywhere in Part IV - the cite and the reasoning are on /writableForm2555Line45PriorYearEarnedIncomeExclusion above. The write-in is complete-safe $0, so on every return that does not use the prior-year rule this fact is arithmetically identical to the printed subtraction.
NO FLOOR AT ZERO, AND THAT IS THE FORM'S OWN SHAPE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Line 45 prints no "If zero or less, enter -0-" instruction - unlike line 33 ("If the result is zero or less, don't complete the rest of this part", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3) and unlike the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet's own lines 2c and 6, which both do print it. A GreaterOf floor here would be an invented rule, so this fact subtracts exactly - no floor on the subtraction and none on the sum - and can go negative if a taxpayer enters line-44 deductions exceeding their line-43 exclusions and the prior-year write-in together. The floor that DOES exist in the chain lives on worksheet line 2c and is the worksheet's fill to write.
WHERE IT GOES - BOTH PRINTED DESTINATIONS. It is a term of /form2555Lines45And50ForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2a below, and of /schedule1Line8dForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion at the foot of this module - which NEGATES it, because Schedule 1 line 8d is a preprinted-parentheses field entered "as a negative number" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 91). Through that leg this figure reduces /agi. Read the sign warning on that fact before summing it anywhere: the positive exclusion lives HERE, the negated entry lives THERE.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, signed (no floor, see above), rounded to whole dollars at this line.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 lines 45 + 50 - the single figure the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 2a reads
Fact.Description:
Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 2a: "Enter the amount from your (and your spouse's if filing jointly) Form 2555, lines 45 and 50" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37). One figure, two Form 2555 lines: line 45 (the two exclusions NET of the line-44 allocable deductions, PLUS the prior-year write-in that line 45 carries) plus line 50 (the housing DEDUCTION).
THE NETTING TRAP, NAMED SO THE WORKSHEET'S FILL CANNOT WALK INTO IT. This figure is ALREADY NET of Form 2555 line 44. Worksheet line 2b - "the total amount of any itemized deductions or exclusions you couldn't claim because they are related to excluded income" - is a DIFFERENT quantity: line 44 is above-the-line deductions ALLOWED in figuring AGI, line 2b is deductions and exclusions DISALLOWED. Subtracting anything derived from line 44 again at worksheet line 2c would double-count it. Worksheet line 2b is its own entry, preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2b; this fact is deliberately not it.
AND IT IS A MIXED QUANTITY, deliberately so, because the worksheet asks for one. It sums an exclusion figure with a DEDUCTION, which is why its name says "lines 45 and 50" rather than anything ending in "exclusion". Form 2441 lines 4/5 name the gross line-43 figure, /form2555Line43Section911TotalExclusions, and Form 8960 line 13 reads /foreignEarnedIncomeExclusion911.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 8d - Form 2555 line 45 entered as a NEGATIVE number (it SUBTRACTS from other income)
Fact.Description:
THIS FACT IS NEGATIVE WHENEVER THE EXCLUSION IS POSITIVE. It is the Schedule 1 line 8d ENTRY, not the exclusion amount: = 0 minus /form2555Line45ExclusionsNetOfAllocableDeductions when /filesForm2555ForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion is true, else $0. Do not sum it anywhere as an exclusion figure - it is the negated one, and a reader who treats it as positive inverts AGI. The positive figures are /form2555Line45ExclusionsNetOfAllocableDeductions and its two siblings above.
THE NEGATION IS THE PRINTED INSTRUCTION, VERBATIM, NOT A MODELLING CHOICE. Schedule 1 line 8d is a preprinted-parentheses field - "Foreign earned income exclusion from Form 2555... 8d ( )" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040s1.pdf, page 1) - and the Form 1040 instructions spell out both halves: "Enter the amount of your foreign earned income and housing exclusion from Form 2555, line 45. Enter the amount in the preprinted parentheses (as a negative number). The amount from Form 2555, line 45, will be subtracted from the other amounts of income listed on lines 8a through 8c and lines 8e through 8z" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 91, a three-column layout in which the left column runs on the odd lines). What is printed is the arithmetic - line 45 "will be subtracted from the other amounts of income" - and subtracting a negative is adding. This fact carries the sign through unchanged rather than inventing a floor the form does not print.
GATED ON THE ATTESTATION - see the block comment above for why that gate is the safety property. Complete-safe: $0 when the gate is false or unanswered, which over-states income and over-taxes (the conservative direction) and keeps every committed scenario byte-identical.

True routes the taxpayer to the line 6a year box; false is what the line 6b box prints. Not itself printed; it is the answer both printed boxes are read from.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 6a last year a Form 2555 was filed
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's Form 2555 Part I line 6a entry: the four digit tax year of the most recent Form 2555 or Form 2555-EZ the taxpayer filed. An Int, printed as typed, the way the qualifying period day counts on lines 31 and 38 are Ints.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 6c Yes box: an exclusion election was revoked
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's Yes answer to line 6c, "Have you ever revoked either of the exclusions?" A revocation under section 911(e)(2) bars a fresh election for the five following tax years without the Secretary's consent, which is why the form asks. Incomplete while unanswered so neither the Yes nor the No box prints.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 6d type of exclusion revoked and the effective tax year
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's Form 2555 line 6d entry, filled only when line 6c is Yes: which exclusion was revoked and the tax year for which the revocation took effect.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 7 country of citizenship or nationality
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's Form 2555 Part I line 7 entry, the country of which the taxpayer is a citizen or national. The graph records whether a filer is a United States citizen or national but not the country name this box prints, so line 7 is its own intake box.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 8a Yes box: a separate foreign residence was maintained for the family
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's Yes answer to line 8a, whether a separate foreign residence was maintained for the family because of adverse living conditions at the tax home. Section 911(c)(3)(B)(ii) is the second foreign household rule this question tests. Incomplete while unanswered so neither box prints.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 8b separate foreign residence and days maintained
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's Form 2555 line 8b entry, filled only when line 8a is Yes: the city and country of the separate foreign residence and the number of days in the tax year that a second household was maintained there. One printed write in box carrying both, so one String.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 9 tax homes, first printed line
Fact.Description: The first of the two printed write in lines on Form 2555 line 9, "List your tax home(s) during your tax year and date(s) established." Line 9 prints two boxes and each is its own String, so a taxpayer with two tax homes fills both.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 9 tax homes, second printed line
Fact.Description: The second of the two printed write in lines on Form 2555 line 9. Left unanswered when the taxpayer had a single tax home, in which case the second printed line stays blank.

Fact.Name: The filer answered at least one Form 2555 Part IV line
Fact.Description: True when any of the sixteen raw Part IV dollar intakes (lines 19, 20a, 20b, 21a through 21d, 22a through 22f, 23, 24 and 25) was answered. This is the "was the source answered" predicate brief rule 3 requires: it selects the computed line 24 and line 27 over the filer typed summary figures, and it is taken on the RAW writables and never on the complete safe wrappers or on the derived totals, every one of which is always Complete and would therefore claim that a filer who never saw Part IV had answered it. That mistake is not cosmetic here: it would give every such return a Complete $0 line 27, a line 41 ceiling of minus line 36, and a zeroed foreign earned income exclusion.

Fact.Name: Any Form 2555 line 19 through 23 component was answered
Fact.Description: True when any of the fourteen raw Part IV dollar intakes that line 24 ADDS was answered: lines 19, 20a, 20b, 21a through 21d, 22a through 22f and 23. It deliberately EXCLUDES /writableForm2555Line24TotalForeignEarnedIncome, the filer typed line 24 total, because this predicate selects the computed line 24 over that attestation and including it would select the computed arm for a filer who typed ONLY the total, giving an Add of zeros and a line 24 of $0. That is not cosmetic: a line 24 of $0 makes line 26 and line 27 $0, forms a line 41 ceiling of minus line 36, and ZEROES A REAL EXCLUSION, which is the exact hazard the Part IV predicate exists to avoid. /form2555PartIvAnswered is the wider predicate and DOES include the typed line 24, because typing a line 24 IS answering Part IV; the two predicates are different questions and must not be merged.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 24 total foreign earned income
Fact.Description: Form 2555 line 24, "Add lines 19 through 21d, line 22g, and line 23", computed from the printed component lines: the complete safe readings of lines 19, 20a, 20b, 21a, 21b, 21c and 21d, plus /form2555Line22gTotalAllowances (itself the Add of the six line 22 allowances), plus line 23. Every operand carries a Min 0 Limit, so the sum is non negative. Computed arm taken whenever /form2555Line24ComponentLinesAnswered. FALLBACK arm: the filer typed line 24 total /writableForm2555Line24TotalForeignEarnedIncome, which is NOT deleted and is what a filer who attests a summary line 24 without itemising Part IV supplies; without that arm such a filer would get an Add of zeros, a $0 line 27 and a zeroed exclusion. Neither arm answered means $0, so this fact is complete safe.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 26, this year's foreign earned income
Fact.Description: Form 2555 line 26, "Subtract line 25 from line 24. Enter the result here and on line 27 on page 3. This is your 2025 foreign earned income". NO FLOOR, faithful to the printed subtraction, in the same spirit as /form2555Line41ForeignEarnedIncomeLessHousingExclusion: line 25 is by its own caption an amount INCLUDED ON LINE 24, so a result below zero is a contradictory pair of entries rather than a modelling case, and floooring it here would hide that. The non negativity that matters is enforced downstream at /foreignEarnedIncomeExclusion911, whose GreaterOf keeps the exclusion itself non negative.

Fact.Name: Form 2555 line 27 has an amount, from Part IV or from the typed entry
Fact.Description: What /foreignEarnedIncomeExclusion911 reads instead of the bare IsComplete of /writableForm2555Line27ForeignEarnedIncome, so that a filer who built Part IV and never typed a summary line 27 still forms the line 41 arm of the line 42 ceiling. It must not be IsComplete of /form2555Line27ForeignEarnedIncome: that alias is complete safe and IsComplete on it is true on every return, which would form a line 41 ceiling of minus line 36 for a filer who reported no foreign earned income at all and zero a real exclusion.
